newsitem.title: FINLAND: HARTWALL SEES "HUGE" POTENTIAL IN BBH.
newsitem.headline: HARTWALL SEES "HUGE" POTENTIAL IN BBH.

text.p: Finnish beverages group Oy Hartwall Ab said on Friday it sees huge growth potential in its joint venture Baltic Beverages Holding AB (BBH), in the Baltic and some other former Soviet Union countries.
"We have huge growth potential in our joint venture," Jussi Lansio, Hartwall managing director Jussi Lansio told an analysts' briefing.
Beer consumption in Russia, which is currently very low mainly due to a lack of supply and capacity, is expected to rise significantly in the future, Lansio said.

Hartwall corporate communications manager Tapio Hedman said there are about 10 times more inhabitants in BBH's market area than in Finland, but beer consumption there is only a fraction of Hartwall's domestic market.

"BBH's growth potential can be described by saying that in Finland there are five million inhabitants who consume about 90 litres beer per person annually. In BBH's market area there are about 50 million consumers ... who drink about 30 litres beer per person annually," Hedman said.
Lansio said BBH will continue to grow also through acquisitions in Russia, as the market there is fragmented with hundreds of small breweries.
In August, BBH acquired 50 percent of Ukrainian brewery Slavutich.
Hartwall on Thursday released January-August results showing a 139.8 million markka profit after financial items, sharply up from 42.4 million in the first eight months in 1995.
Analysts' median forecast profit had been for a 80 million markka (mean 86 million) in a 58 million to 122 million markka range.
Hartwall's operating profit was 163.4 million markka, of which BBH accounted for 76.2 million, Lansio said.
In January-August 1995, Hartwall's operating profit was 68 million markka.
Hartwall holds 50 percent of BBH, and Swedish-Norwegian Pripps-Ringnes AB holds the other half.
